title_en: Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company v. Drug Administration — dispute over administrative penalty for drug management
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative penalty for drug administration; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Jiangsu Province; Legal person; Drug Administration Law; Implementing Rules of the Drug Administration Law; Determination of unlicensed drug production; Jurisdiction over administrative penalty; Qualification of the penalty subject; Uphold the original judgment; Unlicensed production of interferon; Selling counterfeit drugs; Administrative penalty
full_text_en:
Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company v. Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau and Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce — administrative penalty for drug administration dispute

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company.

Legal Representative: Lü Songzhang, General Manager of Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jinheng, Deputy Head of the Rectification and Consolidation Team of Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Hongchao, Attorney at Shanghai United Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau.

Legal Representative: Weng Peiling, Acting Director of Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Lu Xiaoping, Cadre of Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Wu Yannian, Attorney at Shanghai Xuhui District Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce.

Legal Representative: Li Jianyu, Director of Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Ke, Assistant Director of Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce.

The Appellant, Shanghai Global Bioengineering Company, being dissatisfied with the administrative judgment of the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai, appealed to the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court. The court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and, after trial, found the following facts:

The Appellant entered into two contracts on September 18, 1985, and December 11, 1986, with Heqiao Hospital of Yixing City, Jiangsu Province, for joint trial production of "human α-interferon." The contracts provided that the Appellant would provide all technical data for the trial production of "human α-interferon," train operators, supply product labels, and undertake product quality inspection and sales; Heqiao Hospital would provide the site, funds, and raw materials for the product. The profit distribution was: Appellant 55%, Heqiao Hospital 45%. Trial production commenced in early 1987. On February 25, 1988, production was ordered to cease by the Wuxi City Health Bureau. During the trial production period, a total of 23,777 bottles of "human α-interferon" were produced. In April 1988, the Appellee, Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau, discovered in the Pharmaceutical Preparation Department of Xuhui District Central Hospital that the department had in storage "human α-interferon" without an approval number. Upon investigation, it was found that this drug had been produced without authorization by the Appellant and Heqiao Hospital without obtaining a Drug Manufacturing Enterprise License, and without obtaining either an approval number or a trial production number, it was batch-sold and used for therapeutic purposes, directly injected into the human body. As of the time of seizure, the Appellant had sold 23,716 bottles of self-produced "human α-interferon" at a price of RMB 10 per bottle, earning a total profit of RMB 237,160, with 61 bottles remaining seized. The Appellant's share of the profit was RMB 51,353.04. The Appellee, Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau, considered that the Appellant's and Heqiao Hospital's unauthorized production of "human α-interferon" without a license violated the relevant provisions of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. On February 24, 1989, in the name of Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau and Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce, a penalty decision was issued against the Appellant (Heqiao Hospital had been separately dealt with): ordering the Appellant to cease production of "human α-interferon"; confiscating the seized 61 bottles of "human α-interferon" to be destroyed under the supervision of the health administrative authority; confiscating the illegal income of RMB 51,353.04; and imposing a fine of RMB 356,655. The Appellant, dissatisfied with the penalty decision, filed a lawsuit with the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai.

The Appellant alleged that the "human α-interferon" jointly trial-produced with Heqiao Hospital was only for clinical trials, did not enter the circulation channel, and that they intended to apply for a license after successful trial production, rather than unauthorized illegal production, and sought revocation of the administrative penalty decision against it. The Appellees argued that neither the Appellant nor Heqiao Hospital had a Drug Manufacturing Enterprise License, drug production approval number, or trial production number, and they had unauthorizedly produced "human α-interferon" and directly used it on humans, violating the provisions of the Drug Administration Law, and thus should be penalized. Pursuant to Article 51 of the Implementing Rules for the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that where drugs are produced or traded without a Drug Manufacturing Enterprise License or a Drug Trading Enterprise License, the health administrative department shall, in addition to ordering immediate cessation of production or business, confiscate all drugs and illegal income, and impose a fine of not more than five times the price of the genuine drugs produced or traded, depending on the circumstances, the imposition of a fine against the Appellant was correct, and the penalty decision should be upheld.

During the trial at first instance, the Appellant further argued that the production site of "human α-interferon" was in Yixing City, Jiangsu Province, and that the Appellees lacked jurisdiction. The Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau argued that the Appellant's sale of drugs occurred within Shanghai Xuhui District, and according to administrative divisions and administrative management authority, it had the right to supervise the Appellant's conduct. The Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce argued that the Appellant, in addition to violating the Drug Administration Law, had also violated other relevant administrative regulations, and thus it had the authority to investigate and penalize the Appellant.

The court of first instance held that: The Appellant and Heqiao Hospital, after the promulgation and implementation of the Drug Administration Law, produced "human α-interferon" without authorization and without review and approval by the health administrative department, violating the provisions of Article 4 of the Drug Administration Law, which requires that the establishment of a drug manufacturing enterprise must undergo review and approval; their conduct was unlawful. The Appellant's batch sale of "human α-interferon" produced without an approval number violated the provisions of Article 33 of the Drug Administration Law, which prohibits the sale of drugs produced without an approval number; the "human α-interferon" it produced and sold was to be treated as counterfeit drugs in accordance with the law. The Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau, as the drug regulatory authority, had jurisdiction over this case pursuant to Article 45(1) of the Drug Administration Law; pursuant to Article 50 of the Drug Administration Law, which provides that "any person who produces or sells counterfeit drugs shall have the counterfeit drugs and illegal income confiscated and shall be fined," and Article 52 of the same law, which provides that any person who produces or deals in drugs without a Drug Manufacturing Enterprise License shall be ordered to cease production, and all drugs and illegal income shall be confiscated, and a fine may also be imposed, the penalty decision against the Appellant was based on clear facts, reliable evidence, correct application of law, and appropriate penalty. The Appellant's grounds for requesting revocation of the penalty decision were untenable. The Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce, not being a drug regulatory authority, did not have the subject qualification to impose penalties, and when it exercised penalties against the Appellant, it violated the provisions of Article 45(1) of the Drug Administration Law, which vests drug regulatory powers in the health administrative department, constituting ultra vires administration; the Appellant's ground for lawsuit was correct, but this did not affect the correctness of the administrative penalty. Accordingly, the judgment: upheld the part of the administrative penalty decision of the Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Health Bureau that ordered the Appellant to cease production; confiscated illegal income of RMB 51,353.04; imposed a fine of RMB 356,655; and supervised the destruction of the seized 61 bottles of "human α-interferon." Revoked the subject qualification of the Appellee Shanghai Xuhui District Administration for Industry and Commerce in imposing the penalty in that administrative penalty decision.

The Appellant, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court. During the appeal period, the Appellant, after studying the Drug Administration Law and relevant drug administration regulations and rules, realized that its unauthorized production and sale of "human α-interferon" violated legal provisions, expressed acceptance of the penalty imposed by the regulatory authority, and on November 5, 1989, applied to the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court for withdrawal of the appeal. The court of second instance, pursuant to the provisions of Article 3(2) and Article 114 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), which provide that before a judgment is pronounced, whether to permit a plaintiff to withdraw the lawsuit shall be determined by the People's Court, after review, on November 13, 1989, ruled to permit the Appellant to withdraw the appeal and to execute the judgment of first instance.
